paragraphs.source_en: In mid-February of the fourteenth year of Tenshō, Tokugawa Ieyasu sent a secret messenger to Chaya Shirōjirō in the capital, instructing him to order three hundred bolts of cloth.

units.source_zh: 天正十四年二月中旬，德川家康派密使去见京城的茶屋四郎次郎，让茶屋定购布三百匹。

paragraphs.source_en: Before this, acting on orders from Oguri Dairoku, Chaya had ordered a consignment of tiger skins, leopard skins, scarlet woolen cloth, and other goods. He had only just assembled them at Sakai and sent them to Hamamatsu. It must all be for the preparations for his wedding to Lady Asahi—that was the only conclusion he could draw, though he did not fully understand.

What was the purpose of this caution?

paragraphs.source_en: Chaya Shirōjirō happened to catch a boat coming from Fushimi, one of the Yodoya rice boats on its return journey. As he crossed the Yodo River aboard it, he noticed that there were far more boats along both banks than before. Recently, Hideyoshi had placed his favorite retainer Ishida Mitsunari in charge of the Yodo River. More men had been assigned to tow the boats, opening a convenient route even to remote mountain villages. The new castle city of Osaka was linked to this waterway, and the population of the capital was steadily growing as well. It seemed that the peace for which the common people had prayed was at last arriving.
